sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This suit is instituted by the Plaintiff against the defendants for the relief of permanent injunction,
restraining the defendants, their men, supporters, workmen, associates, relatives, assignees and any person claiming under them from interfering with plaintiff's possession and enjoyment of suit property and also restrain them from trespassing into the suit schedule property of plaintiff, and to pass such other reliefs.

2. The case of the plaintiff in brief is as under:
That, suit schedule property which consists of residential and commercial building was originally acquired by father of plaintiff late Muniyappa through registered sale deed dated 09.07.1962.

On 05.11.2013, the father of plaintiff has gifted suit property in favour of plaintiff by executing registered gift deed and same day handed over M Ramachandra vs Srinath Meganath on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74953364/
2 possession of suit property to the plaintiff.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Khata of suit property effected in the name of plaintiff and he is regularly paying tax to concerned authorities in respect of suit property.
The authorities of BDA have made an attempt to grab suit property without following due procedure, as such plaintiff has approached Hon'ble High Court requesting to quash acquisition proceedings.
The Hon'ble High Court has directed to maintain status quo.

The defendants without having right, interest or title over suit property created documents and on 05.03.2018 tried to interfere with plaintiff's possession and enjoyment of suit property and tried to disposes him from suit property.
On these pleadings, the plaintiff has prayed to decree the suit as prayed in plaint.
3. In response to the service of suit summons, the defendant No.1 has tendered his appearance before the court through his counsel and contested the case and filed written statement.
Even after service of suit summons, defendant No.2 has not tendered her appearance before the court and contested the suit, consequently she was placed ex-parte.

4. The contents of written statement of defendant No.1 in brief are as under :-
That, very suit filed by plaintiff is not maintainable and same is bad for mis-joinder of parties.

The plaintiff knowing fully well that, defendant No.2 was outside India on alleged date of cause of action, unnecessarily to harass and humiliate the defendant No.2 she was impleaded as party to the suit.
Very property described in the plaint is not in existence.
The plaintiff with an imaginary boundaries and without any legal foundation has filed present suit with ulterior motive to trespass into property of defendants.
The plaintiff has not come to court with clean hands.
It is denied that,
father
of plaintiff
had acquired suit property through registered sale deed and gifted it in favour of plaintiff.
It is denied that, defendants tried to interfere in plaintiff's possession and enjoyment of suit property.
There is no cause of action for the plaintiff to file present suit.

It is specifically contended that, BDA authorities have acquired land bearing Sy.No.11/3 and Sy.No. 11/2 of Yalakunta Village, thereafter formed layout, which is called as HSR 3rd sector and the defendant No.1 in auction purchased property bearing No.1008.
BDA has executed sale deed dated 27.09.2006 in respect of said property in favour of defendant No.2 as GPA holder of defendant No.1.
During absence of defendants and taking advantage of same, the plaintiff himself as trespassed into property of defendant No.1 and illegally put up shed in property of defendants.
Coming to know about the same, the defendant No.1 has approached the BDA and submitted complaint on 06.07.2017.
The concerned authorities have proceeded to enquire and with help of police removed obstruction on 06.02.2018 put up by plaintiff.
It is the plaintiff who tried to trespass into property of defendants.
On these grounds, it is requested to dismiss the suit.

5. On the basis of above pleadings of both parties, this court has framed the following: :-

sentences.text: 1. Whether the plaintiff proves that he was in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit?
2. Whether the plaintiff proves that the alleged inference of the defendants over the suit schedule property?
3. Whether the plaintiff proves that he is entitled to reliefs as sought for in the plaint?
4. What order or decree?
6. To substantiate the case of the plaintiff, the plaintiff - Ramachandra M., examined himself as PW1 and produced in all 36 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.36.

The defendant No.1- Srinath Meganath examined himself as DW.1 and and produced in all 18 documents as Ex.D1 to Ex.D.18.
7.
I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for plaintiff and learned counsel for defendant and I have perused the case records.

The plaintiff in order to establish his case that, he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit has pleaded, originally Sy.No.11/3 was purchased by his father Muniyappa through registered sale deed dated 09.07.1962.

After purchase of property, name of his father was mutated to Sy.No.11/3 of Yellankute Village and thereafter, Muniyappa had gifted the suit property in favour of plaintiff through registered Gift Deed dated 05.11.2013.
Based on said gift deed, the name of plaintiff mutated to suit property and he is regularly paying taxes pertaining to suit property to concerned authorities.

It is worth to note here that, sale deed dated 09.07.1962 executed by Akkalappa in favour of father of plaintiff late Muniyappa in respect of Sy.No.11/3 to an extent of 1 acre 20 guntas has been produced as per Ex.P.1.
Likewise, gift deed dated 05.11.2013 executed by Muniyappa in favour of plaintiff herein in respect of the suit property and another property has been produced as per Ex.P.2.
The plaintiff has also produced 'B' khata of suit property in his name as per Ex.P.3.
In order to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit property, the plaintiff has produced electricity bills as per Exs.P.4 to P.18 and photographs as per Exs.P.19 to P.28.

Based on these documents, plaintiff has M Ramachandra vs Srinath Meganath on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74953364/
4 pleaded and same is deposed by him who examined as P.W.1 before the court that, his father was original owner of the suit property by virtue of gift deed as per Ex.P.2, he acquired rights and interest in suit property and as on the date of gift deed, possession of suit property handed over him.
As such, he has been continued in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property.
10.

The defendant No.1 in his written statement and the defendant No.1 who examined as D.W.1 in his examination in chief has specifically contended that, the suit schedule property as mentioned in schedule to the plaint is not at all in existence.
The plaintiff has mentioned imaginary boundaries to suit property.
The plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hands, as such he is not entitled for injunctive relief as prayed in plaint.

According to defendant No.1, BDA authorities have acquired land bearing Sy.No.11/2 and 11/3 Yellankunte Village, formed layout and defendant No.1 had purchased property bearing 1008 through sale deed dated 27.09.2006 executed by BDA authorities.
It is further specifically stated by defendant No.1 that, taking undue advantage of absence of defendants, it is the plaintiff who trespass into the property of defendant No.1.

It is evident from contention of defendant No.1 that, he has contended, the plaintiff has not approached the court with clean hands, there is no existence of property as claimed by plaintiff and already Sy.No.11/3 acquired by BDA and formed layout.
Further it is specifically contended by defendant No.1, it is the plaintiff who trespass into the property of defendant No.1 purchased by him from BDA in auction sale.

By contending so, it is specific contention of defendant No.1 that, suit property is not at all in existence, already Sy.No.11/3 of Yellankunte Village was acquired by BDA.
11.

The learned counsel for plaintiff, in support of case of plaintiff has produced documents, such as sale deed, gift deed, khata extract, electricity bills and photographs and based on those documents argued that, plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property.

It is also argued that,
the property bearing No.1008 which defendant No.1 has claimed he purchased from BAD is all together different from suit property and same is existed in Sy.No.11/2.
It is further argued that, the plaintiff having proved his possession and enjoyment over suit property, he is entitled for injunctive relief as prayed for.

The learned counsel for plaintiff in support of his arguments has relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2008) 4 SCC 594 in case of Anathula Sudhakar - Versus - P. Buchi Reddy (Dead) by Lrs and Others, wherein it is held that, "(b) As a suit for injunction simpliciter is concerned only with possession, normally the issue of title will not be directly and substantially in issue.

entities.text: Anathula Sudhakar - Versus - P. Buchi Reddy (Dead) by Lrs and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The prayer for injunction will be decided with reference tot he finding on possession.

But in cases where de jure possession has to be established on the basis of title to the property, as in the case of vacant sites, the issue of title may directly and substantially arise for consideration, as without a finding thereon, it will not be possible to decide the issue of possession.

(c) But a finding on title cannot be recorded in a suit for injunction, unless there are necessary pleadings and appropriate issue regarding title (either specific, or implied as noticed in Annaimuthu Tevar).
Where the averments regarding title
are absent in a plaint and where there is no issue relating to title, the court will not investigate or examine or render a finding on a question of title, in a suit for injunction.

Even where there are necessary pleadings and issue, if the matter involves complicated questions of fact and law relating to title, the court will relegate the parties to the remedy by way of comprehensive suit for declaration of title, instead of deciding the issue in a suit for mere injunction."

M Ramachandra vs Srinath Meganath on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74953364/
5

The learned counsel for plaintiff also relied upon the decision of Hon'ble Bombay High Court reported in (2022) 04 BOM CK 0095 in case of Lalithkumar Jagdishkumar Grover and Others - Versus - New Bandra Hill Co-Operative Housing Society Limited and Others, wherein it is held that,
"In a suit for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with plaintiff's possession, the plaintiff will have to establish that as on the date of the suit he was in lawful possession of the suit property and defendant tried to interfere or disturb such lawful possession.

entities.text: Lalithkumar Jagdishkumar Grover and Others - Versus - New Bandra Hill Co-Operative Housing Society Limited and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the property is a building or building with appurtenant land, there may not be much difficulty in establishing possession.
The plaintiff may prove physical or lawful possession, either of himself or by him through his family members or agents or lessess/licensees.
Even in respect of a land without structures, as for example an agricultural land, possession may be established with reference to the actual use and cultivation.
The question of title is not in issue in such a suit, though it may arise incidentally or collaterally."

The learned counsel for plaintiff has further relied upon the decision reported in ILR 1989 KAR 1701 in case of Gowrishankara Swamigalu - Versus - Siddhaganga Mutt, wherein it is held that, "The preventive remedy of injunction is thus granted as an instant antidote to stop or prevent the invasion of the plaintiff's rights in regard to which a compliant is made.

The court having regard to the expediency involved should not embark upon a nit- picking operation at that stage by holding a mini trial to lay thread-bare the case of the plaintiff to find out if a prima facie case is made out or not.

It would be sufficient if the court is assured that questions raised by the plaintiff are not vexatious or too casual, but are such as to merit serious consideration at a subsequent stage."
12.

In the light of above principles laid down in decision, the plaintiff having approached the court with specific case that, he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property, he has to prove the same before the court.

As already discussed, the claim of plaintiff is that, based on gift deed as per Ex.P.2, he was put in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property and he continued in such lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit.
As contended by defendant, Sy.No.11/2 and 11/3 have been acquired by BDA and acquisition proceedings were initiated.
It is fact that, the defendants have produced the endorsement dated 14.10.2016 issued by BDA as per Ex.D.13.
Another document which is endorsement dated 18.07.2023 issued by BDA is also produced as per Ex.D.12.

On combined appreciation of Exs.D.12 and D.13, it is evident that,
plaintiff has submitted letter to BDA requesting the concerned authority to issue no objection certificate in respect of Sy.No.11/3 to an extent of 1 acre 31 guntas, same was rejected by concerned authority on the ground that, already Sy.No.11/3 to extent of 3 acres 31 gunta was acquired by BDA,
final notification was issued on 28.11.1986 and award in respect of property was also passed.
It is pertinent to note here that, while cross examination of D.W.1, it was suggested by learned counsel for defendant that already Sy.No.11/2 and 11/3 Yellankunte Village were acquired by BDA.
The plaintiff has pleaded his ignorance.
It is also denied by plaintiff that, he approached a SALO and sought for NOC.
The plaintiff has produced certified copy of order passed by Hon'ble High Court in W.P.No.59512/2016 as per Ex.P.30.

Based on the said document, it is contention of plaintiff that,
the Hon'ble High Court has directed to parties to maintain statu-quo with regard to possession of property in question.
Such, the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property.

M Ramachandra vs Srinath Meganath on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74953364/
6 13.
It is pertinent to note here that, the defendant has produced possession certificate issued by BDA in respect of property bearing No.1008 in his favour as per Ex.D.4.
The defendant has also produced copies of proceedings before the BDA as per Exs.D.1 and D.3.
Detailed survey sketch issued by concerned Engineer in respect of Sy.No.11/1, 11/2 and 11/3 of Yellankunte Village has been produced as per Ex D.11.
Based on these documents it is argued on behalf of the learned counsel for defendant that, defendant No.1 has purchased the property bearing No.1008 in auction sale.
Thereafter, taking undue advantage of absence of defendants, plaintiff has illegally entered into possession of property of defendants.
On careful perusal of these documents in sketch it is shown property No.1008 is existed in Sy.No.11/2.
On the same time, as per proceedings before BDA, it is mentioned, there is in structure in Sy.No.1008, Sy.No.1, 2/1, 2/2, 2/3 and 11/2 of Yellankunte Village.

Even if it is made out as per above mentioned documents property of defendant is in Sy.No.11/2, that it is not sufficient to say the plaintiff has proved his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property.
It is plaintiff having approached the court for specific relief of injunction, he has to prove his possession over the suit property independently.

14. As already discussed, there are documents to show way back in the year 1984 the BDA has issued preliminary notification to aquire Sy.No.11/3 to an extent of 3 acres 31 gunta of Yellankunte Village.
Further, on 28.11.1986 final notification was issued and thereafter on 19.01.1989 award was passed and possession of acquired property handed over to Engineer Department of BDA on 30.05.1989.
It is not case of plaintiff that, his father has not received compensation amount in respect of acquired property from BDA.
It is also not case of plaintiff that, his father immediately has challenged notification issued by BDA for acquiring Sy.No.11/3 of Yellankunte Village.
There is no documents or order to shown by such representation the concerned authorities have handed over possession of 1 acre 31 guntas in Sy.No.11/3 in favour of father of plaintiff Muniyappa.
It is fact that, by virtue of final notification and passing of award entire extent of Sy.No.11/3 measuring 3 acres 31 guntas vested with BDA or Government.
As per Ex.P.2 after lapse of nearly 24 years from the date of final notification, Muniyappa executed gift deed in respect of suit property in favour of plaintiff.
In said gift deed is mentioned as on date of gift deed possession of property handover to the plaintiff.
Already discussed as on date of final notification itself entire Sy.No.11/3 vested with Government or BDA.
As on the date of execution of Ex.P.2, executant had no right or authority over suit property as well as he has no possession over the suit property.
Under these circumstances, the contention of plaintiff that, he acquired possession of suit property lawfully by virtue of gift deed executed by his father in his favour is not at all sustainable.

15. Further it is to be noted here, absolutely there is no documents placed on record to show subsequent to final notification, property to an extent of 1 acre 31 guntas in total extent of Sy.No.11/3 was released or returned in favour of plaintiff by BDA.
No doubt it is true, the Hon'ble High Court in W.P.59512/2016 has directed to parties to maintain statu-quo with regard to possession of suit property in question.
As per records, even as on date of order passed by Hon'ble High Court, by virtue of final notification possession of entire extent of Sy.No.11/3 already taken by BDA authorities.

No doubt it is true, the plaintiff has produced electricity bills from the year 1996,
that documents are not sufficient to say the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property.
It is not in case of the plaintiff that, even after acquisition of Sy.No.11/3 of Yellankunte Village, he was continued in unauthorized or illegally possession and enjoyment of the suit property.

M Ramachandra vs Srinath Meganath on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74953364/
7
Taking into to note these facts, it can safely held, plaintiff has failed to prove his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on the date of filing of suit.

Once plaintiff has failed to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit, principle laid down in above decisions relied by the learned counsel for plaintiff are not aptly applicable to facts and circumstances of present case on hand.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the negative.

16. ISSUE NO.2 :- On perusal of documents produced by defendant before the court, it can be gathered, the concerned authorities in its proceedings have observed there is unauthorized structure in Site No.1008 which is belonging to defendant No.1.
As already discussed, plaintiff has failed to prove his lawful possession and enjoyment over suit property as on date of filing of suit.

Once,
plaintiff has failed to establish his possession and enjoyment over suit property, even a it is assumed, the property of defendant is situated in Sy.No.11/2, it can be held that, plaintiff has proved alleged interference by defendants in his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit.
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 in the negative.
17. ISSUE NO.3 :- Already discussed, plaintiff utterly failed to prove that, he is in lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit.
In order to seek injunctive order against defendant as prayed for plaint, first of all plaintiff has to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment over suit property as on date of filing of suit.

The plaintiff having failed to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit and he has not approached the court with clean hands, he is not entitled for highly discretionary relief of injunctive order as prayed in plaint.
The suit filed by the plaintiff is deserves to be dismissed.
Hence, I answer Issue No.3 in the negative.

18. ISSUES No.4 :- In view of the above said findings on Issue Nos. 1 to 3 are in the negative, I proceed to pass the following :-
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed with cost.
Draw decree accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed & computerized by her,
corrected and signed by me and then pronounced in the open Court on this the 9th day of July, 2024).
(BALAPPA APPANNA JARAGU) XXVIII

Once plaintiff has failed to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit, principle laid down in above decisions relied by the learned counsel for plaintiff are not aptly applicable to facts and circumstances of present case on hand.
Once,
plaintiff has failed to establish his possession and enjoyment over suit property, even a it is assumed, the property of defendant is situated in Sy.No.11/2, it can be held that, plaintiff has proved alleged interference by defendants in his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit.
In order to seek injunctive order against defendant as prayed for plaint, first of all plaintiff has to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment over suit property as on date of filing of suit.
The plaintiff having failed to establish his lawful possession and enjoyment of suit property as on date of filing of suit and he has not approached the court with clean hands, he is not entitled for highly discretionary relief of injunctive order as prayed in plaint.
